points.heading: Week overview
points.body:
This week we learn to narrate **when** in Spanish: **one-word** verb forms or **two words** with **haber** plus the participle.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Overview: one word
points.body:
Five **one-word** stations with *cantar*: **canto**, **cantaba**, **canté**, **cantaré**, **cantaría** — same root, different time.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Overview: two words
points.body:
Two-word times always look like **haber** + **-ado/-ido**: *he cantado*, *había comido*; only **haber** changes with I/you/he.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Overview: choosing
points.body:
Choose by asking three questions: Is the past closed? Does the result still matter? Is it background or habit?

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Synthesis
points.body:
If you can build one clear example of each path, you hold the heart of this week’s Spanish times.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

lesson.summary: This week we keep working on: Review Spanish indicative tenses. Read each part calmly and try the activity.
lesson.memoryPhrase: One word: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**. Two words: helper **haber** + already-done form (**he cantado**).
